module Isabelle.Isabelle_Thread

-- | A <a>ThreadId</a> is an abstract type representing a handle to a
--   thread. <a>ThreadId</a> is an instance of <a>Eq</a>, <a>Ord</a> and
--   <a>Show</a>, where the <a>Ord</a> instance implements an arbitrary
--   total ordering over <a>ThreadId</a>s. The <a>Show</a> instance lets
--   you convert an arbitrary-valued <a>ThreadId</a> to string form;
--   showing a <a>ThreadId</a> value is occasionally useful when debugging
--   or diagnosing the behaviour of a concurrent program.
--   
--   <i>Note</i>: in GHC, if you have a <a>ThreadId</a>, you essentially
--   have a pointer to the thread itself. This means the thread itself
--   can't be garbage collected until you drop the <a>ThreadId</a>. This
--   misfeature will hopefully be corrected at a later date.
data () => ThreadId

-- | A result of a thread is either some exception that was thrown in the
--   thread and wasn't catched or the actual value that was returned by the
--   thread.
type Result a = Either SomeException a
find_id :: T -> IO (Maybe ThreadId)
properties :: IO T
change_properties :: (T -> T) -> IO ()
add_resource :: IO () -> IO Unique
del_resource :: Unique -> IO ()
bracket_resource :: IO () -> IO a -> IO a
is_stopped :: IO Bool
expose_stopped :: IO ()
stop :: ThreadId -> IO ()
my_uuid :: IO (Maybe T)
stop_uuid :: T -> IO ()
type Fork a = (ThreadId, T, IO (Result a))
fork_finally :: IO a -> (Either SomeException a -> IO b) -> IO (Fork b)
fork :: IO a -> IO (Fork a)

-- | Various functions on formulas.
module SAD.Data.Formula.Kit

-- | gets rid of top level negation, implication and equivalence if
--   possible. <tt>albet (Not (Ind ..)) == Not (Ind ..)</tt>
albet :: Formula -> Formula

-- | Split a formula <tt>Not (a / b) <i> c </i> ..</tt> into its conjuncts
--   <tt>[a,b,c,..]</tt>
splitConjuncts :: Formula -> [Formula]

-- | remove all tags from a formula
deTag :: Formula -> Formula

-- | Boolean simplification
bool :: Formula -> Formula

-- | perform boolean simplification through the whole formula
boolSimp :: Formula -> Formula

-- | Maybe quantification handles quantification more efficiently in that
--   it possibly already simplifies formulas. Prototype example: "exists x
--   (x = t / P(x))" is replaced by "P(t)" "forall x (x = t =&gt; P(x))" is
--   replaced by "P(t)"
--   
--   In code: <tt>(mbExi "x" (And (Trm TermEquality [Var "x" []
--   Position.none, Var "t" [] Position.none] [] 0) (Var "x" []
--   Position.none))) == Just (Var "t" [] Position.none)</tt> Danger: We
--   ignore the fact that <tt>=</tt> is symmetric.
--   
--   Arguments: the variable to look for (e.g. "x"), whether we are in an
--   "existence" or an "all" case and the formula.
mbBind :: VariableName -> Bool -> Formula -> Maybe Formula
mbExi :: VariableName -> Formula -> Formula
mbAll :: VariableName -> Formula -> Formula
mbpExi :: PosVar -> Formula -> Formula
mbpAll :: PosVar -> Formula -> Formula
mbdExi :: Decl -> Formula -> Formula
mbdAll :: Decl -> Formula -> Formula
blAnd :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
blImp :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
pBlAll :: PosVar -> Formula -> Formula
pBlExi :: PosVar -> Formula -> Formula
mkAll :: VariableName -> Formula -> Formula
mkExi :: VariableName -> Formula -> Formula
pAll :: PosVar -> Formula -> Formula
pExi :: PosVar -> Formula -> Formula
dAll :: Decl -> Formula -> Formula
dExi :: Decl -> Formula -> Formula
zIff :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
zOr :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
mkVar :: VariableName -> Formula

-- | Given a variable name with position data, creates a formula consisting
--   of just a that variable.
pVar :: PosVar -> Formula
mkTrm :: TermId -> TermName -> [Formula] -> Formula
mkEquality :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
mkLess :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
mkThesis :: Formula
mkFunction :: Formula -> Formula
mkMap :: Formula -> Formula
mkApp :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
mkDom :: Formula -> Formula
mkSet :: Formula -> Formula
mkClass :: Formula -> Formula
mkElem :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
mkPair :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
mkObject :: Formula -> Formula

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>truth</tt>
isTop :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>falsity</tt>
isBot :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>not ...</tt>
isNot :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>... and ...</tt>
isAnd :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>... or ...</tt>
isOr :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>... implies ...</tt>
isImp :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>... iff ...</tt>
isIff :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>exists ... such that
--   ...</tt>
isExi :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>for all ... we have
--   ...</tt>
isAll :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is a tagged formula
isTag :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>aObject(...)</tt>
isObject :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>aClass(...)</tt>
isClass :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>aSet(...)</tt>

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>aMap(...)</tt>
isMap :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>aFunction(...)</tt>
isFunction :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>aElementOf(...)</tt>
isElem :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>...(...)</tt>
isApplication :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>Dom(...)</tt>
isDom :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>(...,...)</tt>
isPair :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>iLess(...)</tt>
isLess :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Check whether a formula is of the form <tt>thesis</tt>
isThesis :: Formula -> Bool

-- | Generic tokenization setup
module SAD.Parser.Token

-- | A token of a ForTheL text
data Token
Token :: Text -> T -> Token
[tokenText] :: Token -> Text
[tokenPos] :: Token -> T
EOF :: T -> Token
[tokenPos] :: Token -> T

-- | Render a list of tokens.
renderTokens :: [Token] -> String

-- | A warning: A message equipped with a position that message refers to.
data Warning
Warning :: Text -> T -> Warning

-- | Report several warnings at once.
reportWarnings :: [Warning] -> IO ()

-- | Concatenate a list of tokens/warnings-pairs.
concatTokWarn :: [([Token], [Warning])] -> ([Token], [Warning])

-- | Report a tokenizing error.
handleError :: (error -> (Text, T)) -> ParseErrorBundle [a] error -> IO b

-- | Located error message for an error that is not handled as a custom
--   error of type <a>Error</a> during tokenizing.
unknownError :: (Text, T)

-- | The range in which the tokens lie
tokensRange :: [Token] -> Range

-- | Get the positon of a token, ranging from the beginnig of the first
--   token to the end of the last one.
tokensPos :: [Token] -> T

-- | Concatenate the text components of a list of tokens.
tokensText :: [Token] -> Text

-- | Print a token
showToken :: Token -> Text

-- | Merge a list of tokens into a single token.
mergeTokens :: [Token] -> Token

-- | Append tokens separated by a single space if they were separated by
--   whitespace before
composeTokens :: [Token] -> Text

-- | Determines whether a token is an <i>end of file</i> token
isEOF :: Token -> Bool

-- | A singleton <i>end of file</i> token, i.e. the result of tokenizing an
--   empty document
noTokens :: [Token]
instance GHC.Classes.Ord SAD.Parser.Token.Token
instance GHC.Classes.Eq SAD.Parser.Token.Token


-- | Primitive parsers
module SAD.Parser.Primitives

-- | Parse the current token or return an <tt>EmptyFail</tt> if the input
--   is empty, eof or the supplied test functions returns <tt>Nothing</tt>.
tokenPrim :: (Token -> Maybe a) -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>tokenGuard test p</tt> parses the current token using <tt>p</tt>
--   only if the token passes the predicate <tt>test</tt>. Does not produce
--   particularly useful error messages.
tokenGuard :: (Token -> Bool) -> Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | Parse the end of input
eof :: Parser st ()

-- | Lift possible parse errors into the <tt>ParseResult</tt> using
--   <tt>catchError</tt>.
inspectError :: Parser st a -> Parser st (Either ParseError a)

-- | Map a function over the input in the Parser <tt>State</tt>.
mapInput :: ([Token] -> [Token]) -> Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | Check if the current token satisfies a predicate; if not fail
satisfy :: (Text -> Bool) -> Parser st Text

-- | Always succeed and pass on the string of the token
anyToken :: Parser st Text

-- | Parses a token that is a word (i.e. consists of only alphabetic
--   characters).
word :: Parser st Text

-- | Parse a token that is a digit.
digit :: Parser st Text

-- | Parse a symbolic token, i.e. a TeX command or a single symbolic
--   character
symb :: Parser st Text

-- | <tt>token tok</tt> succeeds iff the current token is equal to
--   <tt>tok</tt>. Consumes the token.
token :: Text -> Parser st ()

-- | Case-insensitive version of <tt>token</tt>. The argument is assumed to
--   be in folded case.
token' :: Text -> Parser st ()

-- | A version of <tt>token'</tt> that returns the position of the token
--   instead of <tt>()</tt>.
tokenPos' :: Text -> Parser st T

-- | <tt>tokenOf toks</tt> succeeds iff the current token is an element of
--   <tt>toks</tt>. Consumes the token.
tokenOf :: [Text] -> Parser st ()

-- | Case-insensitive version of <tt>tokenOf</tt>. All arguments are
--   assumed to be in folded case.
tokenOf' :: [Text] -> Parser st ()

-- | A sequence of tokens.
tokenSeq :: [Text] -> Parser st ()

-- | Case-insensitive version of <tt>tokenSeq</tt>. All arguments are
--   assumed to be in folded case.
tokenSeq' :: [Text] -> Parser st ()

-- | <tt>tokenSeqOf tokSeqs</tt> succeeds iff one of the token sequences in
--   <tt>tokSeq</tt> can be consumed.
tokenSeqOf :: [[Text]] -> Parser st ()

-- | Case-insensitive version of <tt>tokenSeqOf</tt>. All arguments are
--   assumed to be in folded case.
tokenSeqOf' :: [[Text]] -> Parser st ()
getToken :: Text -> Parser st Text
getToken' :: Text -> Parser st Text

-- | <tt>tokenOf toks</tt> succeeds iff the current token is an element of
--   <tt>toks</tt>. Returns the parsed token.
getTokenOf :: [Text] -> Parser st Text

-- | Case-insensitive version of <tt>getTokenOf</tt>. All arguments are
--   assumed to be in folded case.
getTokenOf' :: [Text] -> Parser st Text

-- | Check if the next tokens are the (case-sensitive) characters of the
--   input string. Useful for parsing symbols.
symbol :: Text -> Parser st ()

-- | Same as <a>symbol</a> but the token to be parsed must not be prepended
--   by a white token.
symbolNotAfterSpace :: Text -> Parser st ()


-- | Parser combinators.
module SAD.Parser.Combinators

-- | Choose with lookahead.
(</>) :: Parser st a -> Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | Try a parser with lookahead.
try :: Parser st a -> Parser st a
(-|-) :: forall st a. Parser st a -> Parser st a -> Parser st a
infixr 2 -|-

-- | Parse one or more <tt>a</tt>s interleaved by <tt>sep</tt>s keeping all
--   intermediary results.
sepBy :: Parser st a -> Parser st sep -> Parser st [a]

-- | Parse zero or more <tt>a</tt>s interleaved by <tt>sep</tt>s keeping
--   all intermediary results.
sepBy0 :: Parser st a -> Parser st sep -> Parser st [a]

-- | Same as <a>sepBy</a> but keep only the largest result.
sepByLL1 :: Parser st a -> Parser st sep -> Parser st [a]

-- | <tt>opt x p</tt> runs both <tt>p</tt> and <tt>x</tt> and combines
--   their errors and results.
opt :: a -> Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>optLL1 x p</tt> will run <tt>p</tt>; if <tt>p</tt> fails without
--   consuming any input it will return <tt>x</tt>.
optLL1 :: a -> Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>optLLx x p</tt> will try <tt>p</tt>; if <tt>p</tt> fails it will
--   return <tt>x</tt>.
optLLx :: a -> Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | Run the parser as often as possible keeping all intermediary results.
chain :: Parser st a -> Parser st [a]

-- | Run the parser as often as possible keeping only the longest result.
chainLL1 :: Parser st a -> Parser st [a]
after :: Parser st a -> Parser st b -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>enclosed begin end p</tt> parses <tt>begin</tt>, followed by
--   <tt>p</tt>, followed by <tt>end</tt>, returning the result of
--   <tt>p</tt> and its range.
enclosed :: Text -> Text -> Parser st a -> Parser st (Range, a)

-- | <tt>texCommand name</tt> parses <tt>"\" <a>name</a></tt>.
texCommand :: Text -> Parser st ()
texCommandPos :: Text -> Parser st T

-- | <tt>texCommandWithArg name arg</tt> parses <tt>"\" <a>name</a> "{"
--   <a>arg</a> "}"</tt>.
texCommandWithArg :: Text -> Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>optInTexArg macroName p</tt> runs either <tt>p</tt>, or <tt>"\"
--   <a>macroname</a> "{" <a>p</a> "}"</tt>.
optInTexArg :: Text -> Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>texBegin env</tt> parses <tt>"\begin" "{" <a>env</a> "}"</tt>.
texBegin :: Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>texBegin env</tt> parses <tt>"\end" "{" <a>env</a> "}"</tt>.
texEnd :: Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>parenthesised p</tt> parses @"(" <a>p</a> ")".
parenthesised :: Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>bracketed p</tt> parses @"[" <a>p</a> "]".
bracketed :: Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>braced p</tt> parses <tt>"{" <a>p</a> "}"</tt>.
braced :: Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>braced p</tt> parses <tt>"{" <a>p</a> "}"</tt>.
bracedOrTexBraced :: Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>optParenthesised p</tt> parses <tt><a>p</a> | "(" <a>p</a>
--   ")"</tt>.
optParenthesised :: Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>optBraced p</tt> parses <tt><a>p</a> | "{" <a>p</a> "}"</tt>.
optBraced :: Parser st a -> Parser st a
pathComponent :: Parser st FilePath
path :: Parser st FilePath

-- | Parses <tt>"."</tt>.
dot :: Parser st Range

-- | <tt>finish p</tt> parses <tt><a>p</a> "."</tt>.
finish :: Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>repeatUntil' step end</tt> repeats a monadic action <tt>step</tt>
--   until <tt>end</tt> succeeds.
repeatUntil' :: (MonadPlus m, Monoid a) => m a -> m b -> m (a, b)

-- | Like <tt>repeatUntil'</tt>, but aggregates the results with the monoid
--   operation.
repeatUntil :: (MonadPlus m, Monoid a) => m a -> m a -> m a

-- | If <tt>p</tt> is ambiguous, <tt>narrow p</tt> fails and reports a
--   well-formedness error.
narrow :: Show a => Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | If <tt>p</tt> is ambiguous, <tt>narrow p</tt> fails and reports a
--   well-formedness error.
narrow2 :: Show b => Parser st (a, b) -> Parser st (a, b)

-- | Only take the longest possible parses (by <tt>SourcePos</tt>), discard
--   all others.
takeLongest :: Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | <tt>failing p</tt> fails if <tt>p</tt> succeeds.
failing :: Parser st a -> Parser st ()

-- | Labeling of production rules for better error messages.
(<?>) :: Parser st a -> Text -> Parser st a
infix 0 <?>

-- | Labeling of production rules for better error messages. (<tt>label msg
--   p = p <a>?</a> msg</tt>)
label :: Text -> Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | Fail with a well-formedness error.
failWF :: Text -> Parser st a

-- | Do not produce an error message.
noError :: Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | Parse and keep only results well-formed according to the supplied
--   check; fail if there are none. Here <tt>Just str</tt> signifies an
--   error.
wellFormedCheck :: (a -> Maybe Text) -> Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | Parse and keep only results well-formed according to the supplied
--   check; fail if there are none with a normal error (and not a
--   well-formedness one). Here <tt>True</tt> means well-formed.
lexicalCheck :: (a -> Bool) -> Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | In case of failure print the error, in case of success print the
--   result of the function shw. This function is implemented using the
--   impure function <tt>Debug.Trace.trace</tt> and should only be used for
--   debugging purposes.
errorTrace :: Text -> (ParseResult st a -> Text) -> Parser st a -> Parser st a

-- | Return <tt>()</tt> if the next token isn't <tt>EOF</tt>.
notEof :: Parser st ()


-- | FoTheL state and state management, parsing of primitives, operations
--   on variables and macro expressions.
module SAD.ForTheL.Base

-- | Parser for ForTheL texts
type FTL = Parser FState

-- | Unary terms.
type UTerm = (Formula -> Formula, Formula)

-- | Unary notions.
type UNotion = (Formula -> Formula, Formula, PosVar)

-- | Multi-terms.
type MTerm = (Formula -> Formula, [Formula])

-- | Multi-notions.
type MNotion = (Formula -> Formula, Formula, Set PosVar)
type Prim = ([Pattern], [Formula] -> Formula)

-- | ForTheL state
data FState
FState :: [Prim] -> [Prim] -> [Prim] -> [Prim] -> [Prim] -> [Prim] -> [Prim] -> [Prim] -> [Prim] -> [Prim] -> [Prim] -> [Prim] -> [TVar] -> [[Text]] -> Set VariableName -> Int -> Int -> Int -> [Report] -> Context -> FState

-- | adjective expressions
[adjectiveExpr] :: FState -> [Prim]

-- | verb expressions
[verbExpr] :: FState -> [Prim]

-- | notion expressions
[notionExpr] :: FState -> [Prim]

-- | symbolic notion expressions
[symbNotionExpr] :: FState -> [Prim]

-- | circumfix funxtion expressions
[cfnExpr] :: FState -> [Prim]

-- | right funxtion expressions
[rfnExpr] :: FState -> [Prim]

-- | left funxtion expressions
[lfnExpr] :: FState -> [Prim]

-- | infix function expressions
[ifnExpr] :: FState -> [Prim]

-- | circumfix predicate expressions
[cprExpr] :: FState -> [Prim]

-- | right predicate expressions
[rprExpr] :: FState -> [Prim]

-- | left predicate expressions
[lprExpr] :: FState -> [Prim]

-- | infix predicate expressions
[iprExpr] :: FState -> [Prim]

-- | pretyped variables
[tvrExpr] :: FState -> [TVar]

-- | synonyms
[strSyms] :: FState -> [[Text]]
[varDecl] :: FState -> Set VariableName
[idCount] :: FState -> Int
[hiddenCount] :: FState -> Int
[serialCounter] :: FState -> Int
[reports] :: FState -> [Report]
[program] :: FState -> Context

-- | Initial state of the parsing process. Provides the following
--   predefined expressions:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><tt>"equal" "to" ...</tt> (notion expression)</li>
--   <li><tt>"nonequal" "to" ...</tt> (notion expression)</li>
--   <li><tt>"map" | "maps"</tt> (notion expression)</li>
--   <li><tt>"function" | "functions"</tt> (notion expression)</li>
--   <li><tt>"set" | "sets"</tt> (notion expression)</li>
--   <li><tt>"class" | "classes" | "collection" | "collections"</tt>
--   (notion expression)</li>
--   <li><tt>(["mathematical"] ("object" | "objects")) | "element" |
--   "elements"</tt> (notion expression)</li>
--   <li><tt>("element" | "elements") "of" ...</tt> (notion
--   expression)</li>
--   <li><tt>"(" ... "," ... ")"</tt> (function expression)</li>
--   <li><tt>"...(...)</tt>" (function expression)</li>
--   </ul>
initFState :: Context -> FState
getExpr :: (FState -> [a]) -> (a -> FTL b) -> FTL b
getDecl :: FTL (Set VariableName)

-- | <tt>addDecl vs p</tt> temporarily modifies the variable declarations
--   to include <tt>vs</tt> while running the parser <tt>p</tt>.
addDecl :: Set VariableName -> FTL a -> FTL a
getPretyped :: FTL [TVar]
makeDecl :: PosVar -> FTL Decl
makeDecls :: Set PosVar -> FTL (Set Decl)
declared :: MNotion -> FTL (Formula -> Formula, Formula, Set Decl)
primVer :: FTL UTerm -> FTL UTerm
primAdj :: FTL UTerm -> FTL UTerm
primUnAdj :: FTL UTerm -> FTL UTerm
primPrd :: FTL (b1 -> b1, Formula) -> ([Pattern], [Formula] -> b2) -> FTL (b1 -> b1, b2)
primMultiVer :: FTL UTerm -> FTL UTerm
primMultiAdj :: FTL UTerm -> FTL UTerm
primMultiUnAdj :: FTL UTerm -> FTL UTerm
primMultiPredicate :: FTL (b1 -> b1, Formula) -> ([Pattern], [Formula] -> b2) -> FTL (b1 -> b1, b2)
primNotion :: FTL UTerm -> FTL MNotion
primOfNotion :: FTL UTerm -> FTL MNotion
primCommonNotion :: FTL UTerm -> FTL MTerm -> FTL MNotion
primFun :: FTL UTerm -> FTL UTerm
primCpr :: FTL Formula -> FTL Formula
primRpr :: FTL Formula -> FTL (Formula -> Formula)
primLpr :: FTL Formula -> FTL (Formula -> Formula)
primIpr :: FTL Formula -> FTL (Formula -> Formula -> Formula)
primCfn :: FTL Formula -> FTL Formula
primRfn :: FTL Formula -> FTL (Formula -> Formula)
primLfn :: FTL Formula -> FTL (Formula -> Formula)
primIfn :: FTL Formula -> FTL (Formula -> Formula -> Formula)
primCsm :: FTL a -> ([Pattern], [a] -> b) -> FTL b
primRsm :: FTL a -> ([Pattern], [a] -> t) -> FTL (a -> t)
primLsm :: FTL a -> ([Pattern], [a] -> t) -> FTL (a -> t)
primIsm :: FTL a -> ([Pattern], [a] -> t) -> FTL (a -> a -> t)
primSnt :: FTL Formula -> FTL MNotion
data Pattern
Word :: [Text] -> Pattern
Symbol :: Text -> Pattern
Vr :: Pattern
Nm :: Pattern

-- | Adding error reporting to pattern parsing.
patternTokenOf' :: [Text] -> FTL ()
patternSymbolTokenOf :: Text -> FTL ()

-- | Most basic pattern parser: simply follow the pattern and parse terms
--   with p at variable places
wdPattern :: FTL (b -> b, a) -> [Pattern] -> FTL (b -> b, [a])

-- | Parse a symbolic pattern.
symbolPattern :: FTL a -> [Pattern] -> FTL [a]

-- | Parse a multi-subject pattern: follow the pattern, but ignore the
--   token' right before the first variable. Then check that all "and"
--   tokens have been consumed. Example pattern: [Word
--   ["commute","commutes"], Word ["with"], Vr]. Then we can parse "a
--   commutes with c and d" as well as "a and b commute".
multiPattern :: FTL (b -> b, a) -> [Pattern] -> FTL (b -> b, [a])
notionPattern :: FTL (b -> b, a) -> [Pattern] -> FTL (b -> b, Set PosVar, [a])
ofPattern :: FTL (b -> b, a) -> [Pattern] -> FTL (b -> b, Set PosVar, [a])

-- | parse a "common"-notion: basically like the above. We use the special
--   parser s for the first variable place after the "of" since we expect
--   multiple terms here. Example: A common *divisor of m and n*.
commonPattern :: FTL (b -> b, a1) -> FTL (b -> c, [a2]) -> [Pattern] -> FTL (b -> c, Set PosVar, [a2], [a1])
naPattern :: FTL (b -> b, a) -> [Pattern] -> FTL (b -> b, [a])
nameList :: FTL (Set PosVar)
varList :: FTL (Set PosVar)
nodups :: IsVar a => [a] -> FTL (Set a)
hidden :: FTL PosVar

-- | Parse the next token as a variable (a sequence of alpha-num chars
--   beginning with an alpha) and return (<tt>x</tt> + the sequence) with
--   the current position.
var :: FTL PosVar
type TVar = (Set VariableName, Formula)
primTypedVar :: FTL MNotion
freeVars :: IsVar a => Formula -> FTL (FV a)

-- | Produce the variables declared by a formula together with their
--   positions. As parameter we pass the already known variables.
decl :: IsVar a => Formula -> FV a
declNames :: Set VariableName -> Formula -> Set VariableName

-- | Produce the bindings in a formula in a Decl data type and take care of
--   the serial counter.
bindings :: Set VariableName -> Formula -> FTL (Set Decl)
freeOrOverlapping :: Set VariableName -> Formula -> Maybe Text
iffPhrases :: [[Text]]
standForPhrases :: [[Text]]

-- | Keywords not allowed as variable names
keywords :: [Text]
greek :: [Text]
lowerGreek :: [Text]
varGreek :: [Text]
upperGreek :: [Text]

-- | Print a variable (just for now).
showVar :: VariableName -> Text
instance GHC.Show.Show SAD.ForTheL.Base.Pattern
instance GHC.Classes.Eq SAD.ForTheL.Base.Pattern


-- | Document parsing.
module SAD.ForTheL.Structure

-- | This is the last step when creating a proof text from a top-level
--   section. We take some metadata and moreover read some metadata from
--   the state and use it to make a <a>ProofText</a> out of the content and
--   (optional) label of a top-level section.
addMetadata :: Section -> [ProofText] -> Maybe Text -> FTL ProofText

-- | Parse an identifier, i.e. a sequence of alphanumeric tokens and
--   underscores.
identifier :: FTL Text

-- | Finish a statement without a link.
finishWithoutLink :: FTL [a]
updateDeclbefore :: FTL ProofText -> FTL [ProofText] -> FTL [ProofText]
pretyping :: Block -> FTL Block
pret :: Set VariableName -> [TVar] -> Block -> FTL Block
pretypeBefore :: FTL Block -> FTL [ProofText] -> FTL [ProofText]

-- | <tt>pretype p</tt> prepends a <tt>ProofText</tt> to <tt>p</tt> that
--   explicitly declares the pretypings and the variable declarations
--   contained in the parser state before running <tt>p</tt>. Moreover the
--   this pretyping information is also added as a <tt>ProofText</tt>.
pretype :: FTL Block -> FTL [ProofText]

-- | <pre>
--   [ "then" | "hence" | "thus" | "therefore" | "consequently" ]
--   </pre>
hence :: FTL ()

-- | <pre>
--   [ ("let" "us") | ("we" "can") ]
--   </pre>
letUs :: FTL ()

-- | Header for choice expressions: <tt>[ <a>hence</a> ] [ <a>letUs</a> ]
--   ("choose" | "take" | "consider")</tt>
choiceHeader :: FTL ()

-- | Header for affirmation: <tt><a>hence</a></tt>
affirmationHeader :: FTL ()

-- | Header for assumption: @"let" | (<a>letUs</a> ("assume" | "presume" |
--   "suppose") ["that"])
assumptionHeader :: FTL ()

-- | Low-leve definition header: <tt>"define"</tt>
lowLevelDefinitionHeader :: FTL ()
statementBlock :: Section -> FTL Formula -> FTL [Text] -> FTL Block
statementBlock' :: Section -> FTL (a, Formula) -> FTL [Text] -> FTL (a, Block)
pretypeSentence :: Section -> FTL Formula -> (Set VariableName -> Formula -> Maybe Text) -> FTL [Text] -> FTL Block
pretypeSentence' :: Section -> FTL (a, Formula) -> (Set VariableName -> Formula -> Maybe Text) -> FTL [Text] -> FTL (a, Block)
sentence :: Section -> FTL Formula -> (Set VariableName -> Formula -> Maybe Text) -> FTL [Text] -> FTL Block
defVars :: Set VariableName -> Formula -> Maybe Text
assumeVars :: Set VariableName -> Formula -> Maybe Text
affirmVars :: Set VariableName -> Formula -> Maybe Text
llDefnVars :: Set VariableName -> Formula -> Maybe Text

-- | Proof scheme
data Scheme

-- | No proof
None :: Scheme

-- | Confirmation ("Indeed ... .")
Short :: Scheme

-- | Proof without special method
Raw :: Scheme

-- | Proof by contradiction
Contradiction :: Scheme

-- | Proof by induction
InS :: Scheme

-- | Term to induce on (in a proof by induction)
InT :: Formula -> Scheme

-- | Low-level theorem header: <tt><a>letUs</a> ("prove" | "show" |
--   "demonstrate") [<a>byProofMethod</a>] "that"</tt>
letUsShowThat :: FTL Scheme

-- | By proof method: <tt>"by" <a>method</a></tt>
byProofMethod :: FTL Scheme

-- | Proof method: <tt>"contradiction" | "case" "analysis" | "induction"
--   ["on" <a>sTerm</a>]</tt>
proofMethod :: FTL Scheme

-- | Creation of induction thesis.
indThesis :: Formula -> Scheme -> Scheme -> FTL Formula
instance GHC.Show.Show SAD.ForTheL.Structure.Scheme
instance GHC.Classes.Ord SAD.ForTheL.Structure.Scheme
instance GHC.Classes.Eq SAD.ForTheL.Structure.Scheme


-- | Main text reading functions.
module SAD.Import.Reader

-- | Parse one or more ForTheL texts
readProofText :: ParserKind -> [ProofText] -> IO [ProofText]


-- | Generation of proof tasks for low-level map and class definitions and
--   choices.
module SAD.Core.ProofTask
generateProofTask :: Section -> Set VariableName -> Formula -> Formula


-- | This is a re-export of the relevant parts of SAD's API which means
--   that the rest can remain out of the 'exposed-modules'. That allows us
--   to detect unnecessary exports and leads to better encapsulation.
module SAD.API
data Counter
Sections :: Counter
Goals :: Counter
FailedGoals :: Counter
TrivialGoals :: Counter
SuccessfulGoals :: Counter
Symbols :: Counter
TrivialChecks :: Counter
HardChecks :: Counter
SuccessfulChecks :: Counter
Unfolds :: Counter
Equations :: Counter
FailedEquations :: Counter
data Timer
ProofTimer :: Timer
SuccessTimer :: Timer
SimplifyTimer :: Timer
showTimeDiff :: NominalDiffTime -> String
sumCounter :: [Tracker] -> Counter -> Int
sumTimer :: [Tracker] -> Timer -> NominalDiffTime
maximalTimer :: [Tracker] -> Timer -> NominalDiffTime
reports_text :: [Report_Text] -> IO ()
report_text :: T -> T -> Bytes -> IO ()
reports :: [Report] -> IO ()
report :: T -> T -> IO ()
console_position :: T -> Bytes
show_position :: T -> String
origin_main :: Bytes
origin_export :: Bytes
origin_forthel :: Bytes
origin_parser :: Bytes
origin_reasoner :: Bytes
origin_simplifier :: Bytes
origin_thesis :: Bytes
origin_translate :: Bytes
origin_reader :: Bytes
data Kind
STATE :: Kind
WRITELN :: Kind
INFORMATION :: Kind
TRACING :: Kind
WARNING :: Kind
LEGACY_FEATURE :: Kind
ERROR :: Kind
output :: BYTES a => Bytes -> Kind -> T -> a -> IO ()
error :: BYTES a => Bytes -> T -> a -> IO b
outputMain :: BYTES a => Kind -> T -> a -> IO ()
outputExport :: BYTES a => Kind -> T -> a -> IO ()
outputForTheL :: BYTES a => Kind -> T -> a -> IO ()
outputParser :: BYTES a => Kind -> T -> a -> IO ()
outputReasoner :: BYTES a => Kind -> T -> a -> IO ()
outputThesis :: BYTES a => Kind -> T -> a -> IO ()
outputSimplifier :: BYTES a => Kind -> T -> a -> IO ()
outputTranslate :: BYTES a => Kind -> T -> a -> IO ()
outputTokenizer :: BYTES a => Kind -> T -> a -> IO ()
errorExport :: BYTES a => T -> a -> IO b
errorParser :: BYTES a => T -> a -> IO b
errorLexer :: BYTES a => T -> a -> IO b
errorTokenizer :: BYTES a => T -> a -> IO b
errorReader :: BYTES a => T -> a -> IO b

-- | verify proof text (document root)
verifyRoot :: Cache -> Cache -> T -> [ProofText] -> IO (Bool, [Tracker])
data Instr
Command :: Command -> Instr
Synonym :: [Text] -> Instr
SetBool :: T Bool -> Bool -> Instr
SetInt :: T Int -> Int -> Instr
SetBytes :: T Bytes -> Bytes -> Instr
GetRelativeFilePath :: FilePath -> Instr
GetAbsoluteFilePath :: FilePath -> Instr
GetModule :: FilePath -> FilePath -> String -> Instr
GetText :: Bytes -> Instr
Verbose :: Bool -> Instr

-- | Indicate which of the parsers is currently used. This is must be
--   recorded in the State for read instruction to work properly.
data ParserKind
Ftl :: ParserKind
Tex :: ParserKind
Stex :: ParserKind
getInstr :: T a -> [Instr] -> a
data ProofText
ProofTextBlock :: Block -> ProofText
ProofTextInstr :: T -> Instr -> ProofText
ProofTextDrop :: T -> Drop -> ProofText
ProofTextSynonym :: T -> ProofText
ProofTextPretyping :: T -> Set PosVar -> ProofText
ProofTextMacro :: T -> ProofText
ProofTextError :: ParseError -> ProofText
parseErrors :: ProofText -> [ParseError]

-- | Parse one or more ForTheL texts
readProofText :: ParserKind -> [ProofText] -> IO [ProofText]
errorPos :: ParseError -> T

-- | A first-order formula, term or de Brujin index
data Formula
data ForthelExpr
ForthelExpr :: Text -> [Formula] -> Bool -> Bool -> Bool -> Formula -> ForthelExpr
[forthelName] :: ForthelExpr -> Text
[forthelAssumptions] :: ForthelExpr -> [Formula]
[forthelTopLevel] :: ForthelExpr -> Bool
[forthelNeedsProof] :: ForthelExpr -> Bool
[forthelCanDeclare] :: ForthelExpr -> Bool
[forthelFormula] :: ForthelExpr -> Formula
extractBlocks :: ProofText -> Forest ForthelExpr
toStatement :: Tree ForthelExpr -> Either Text ForthelExpr
pattern (:\/) :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
pattern (:/\) :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
pattern (:->) :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
pattern (:<->) :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
pattern (:==) :: Formula -> Formula -> Formula
toDeclaration :: ForthelExpr -> Declaration
varToText :: VariableName -> Text
termToText :: TermName -> Text
toLeanCode :: [ForthelExpr] -> Text
ppForthelExpr :: ForthelExpr -> String
debugShow :: Formula -> String
parens :: String -> String


-- | Main application entry point: Terminal or PIDE mode.
module SAD.Main
main :: IO ()
mainTerminal :: [Instr] -> [String] -> IO ()
usageHeader :: String
mainPIDE :: [Instr] -> IO ()
pideServer :: Cache -> Cache -> [Instr] -> Socket -> IO ()
lexInputText :: ParserKind -> Bytes -> IO Int
tokenizeInputText :: ParserKind -> Bytes -> IO Int
translateInputText :: ParserKind -> [ProofText] -> IO Int
verifyInputText :: ParserKind -> Cache -> Cache -> [ProofText] -> IO Int
renderInputFile :: FilePath -> FilePath -> FilePath -> IO Int
readArgs :: [String] -> IO ([Instr], [String])
optParam :: [Char] -> T a -> ArgDescr b -> String -> OptDescr b
optSwitch :: [Char] -> T Bool -> Bool -> Bytes -> OptDescr Instr
optFlag :: [Char] -> T Bool -> OptDescr Instr
optNat :: [Char] -> T Int -> OptDescr Instr
optArgument :: [Char] -> T Bytes -> String -> OptDescr Instr
options :: [OptDescr Instr]
